  1. internal/server/server.go includes route registration, readonly checks, payload binding, and direct domain invocation.

Impact:

  1. Repetition across many endpoints.
  2. Harder testing and policy consistency.

Remediation priority: P1

Recommended actions:

  1. Introduce dedicated middleware/policy gates for write operations.
  2. Move endpoint orchestration into service methods.

docs.title: 5. Test coverage is narrow for critical paths
docs.text:
Evidence:

  1. Backend tests are limited; only a small number of package tests exist.
  2. Snapshot regression test exists in tests/regression.test.ts but requires local toolchain not available in this environment.

Impact:

  1. Refactors risk behavioral regressions.
  2. Security and concurrency regressions are likely to slip.

Remediation priority: P2

Recommended actions:

  1. Add service-level unit tests for sync/auth/error paths.
  2. Add API integration tests for auth, readonly mode, and editor write paths.
  3. Add security-focused tests for token handling and brute-force controls.

docs.title: 6. Config state is global and mutable
docs.text:
Evidence:

  1. Config singleton is process-global in internal/config/config.go.

Impact:

  1. Limits test isolation.
  2. Potential race and coupling risks as concurrency increases.

Remediation priority: P2

Recommended actions:

  1. Introduce immutable config snapshots and dependency injection.
  2. Avoid hidden global reads in deep domain layers.

docs.title: Observed Strengths
docs.text:
1. Clear domain-oriented package structure in internal/.
  2. Shared backend across web and desktop reduces feature divergence.
  3. Path traversal mitigation helper exists (BuildSubPath in internal/utils/utils.go).
  4. Config schema validation and docs are already mature for user-facing configuration.

docs.title: Validation Limits
docs.text:
1. Could not execute go test ./... because go is unavailable in current terminal environment.
  2. Could not execute frontend checks because svelte-kit dependencies are unavailable in current terminal environment.

These runtime/toolchain checks should be re-run in CI or a fully provisioned dev machine as part of remediation.

docs.title: Expenses
docs.text:
Paisa provides multiple dedicated views to track day-to-day spending, spot seasonality, compare month-over-month and year-over-year changes, and trace where outflows go.

In the default Grouped navigation layout, expense tools live under Cash Flow → Expenses & Budget. In the Classic layout, they appear under the top-level Expenses menu.

docs.title: Monthly Expenses
docs.text:
Route: /expense/monthly

The Monthly Expenses page combines monthly summary metrics, interactive visualizations, spending trends, and the transaction list for the selected month:

  • Summary KPIs: Displays Gross Income, Tax, Net Investment, and Expenses for the selected month (along with net income, tax rate, savings rate, and expense rate percentages).
  • Daily Expense Calendar: Shows daily spending totals and per-category donut rings across the selected calendar month. Hover over any day to inspect individual postings.
  • Category Breakdown: Horizontal bar chart ranking level-2 expense categories (Expenses:<Category>) for the selected month.
  • Spending Trends: Compares category-level spending between two periods and renders a 6-month sparkline per category (with the latest bar highlighted and a dashed average line). Use the toggle in the top-right corner of the trends box to switch between:
  • Last 30 Days (default) — compares the rolling last 30 days against the preceding 30-day window.
  • Calendar Month — compares the currently selected calendar month (e.g., from the Month Picker or by clicking a bar in the monthly timeline) against the immediately preceding calendar month. The active current month is marked (MTD), and each sparkline anchors at the selected month. Your selected comparison mode is saved in browser storage (localStorage).
  • Monthly Expenses Timeline: Stacked monthly bar chart filtered by the navbar date range selector. Clicking any bar selects that month across the calendar, breakdown, expense list, and Calendar Month trends; clicking a legend item filters to a single category.
  • Responsive Mobile Layout: On mobile viewports, the summary KPIs and analytical widgets (calendar, category breakdown, spending trends, and timeline) appear first at the top of the page, followed by the individual list of Expenses postings for the selected month.

Expenses:Tax postings are excluded from expense trend calculations so tax payments do not distort living-cost trends.

docs.title: Yearly Expenses
docs.text:
Route: /expense/yearly

The Yearly Expenses view summarizes spending across an entire financial year (selectable via the Financial Year Picker in the sub-navigation bar):

  • Displays annual Gross Income, Tax, Net Investment, and Expenses KPIs.
  • Provides a 12-month mini-calendar grid, annual category breakdown bar chart, and stacked multi-year timeline.

docs.title: Expense Breakdown (Sankey)
docs.text:
Route: /expense/sankey

Expense Breakdown renders a Sankey flow diagram restricted exclusively to links that terminate in Expenses:* accounts over the selected navbar date range, along with Total Inflow and Total Outflow summary figures.

To analyze full-path flows across Income, Assets, Liabilities, and Expenses (including transfers and account-depth aggregation), see Cash Flow – Money Flow (Sankey).

docs.title: Spending Heatmap & Seasonality
docs.text:
Route: /expense/heatmap

The Heatmap page visualizes daily and seasonal spending patterns using GET /api/expense/daily:

  • Filters: Choose a calendar Year, filter by Category (or All categories), and switch between Day-wise and Week-wise intensity grids.
  • KPI Cards: Shows Total spend, Active spend days (with average spend per calendar day), Peak day, and Strongest pattern (peak month and weekday average).
  • Seasonality Charts:
  • Average spend by weekday — highlights day-of-week habits (e.g., weekend spikes).
  • Seasonality by month — compares average monthly totals across January–December.

docs.title: Month-over-Month (MoM)
docs.text:
Route: /expense/mom

The Month-over-Month (MoM) diagnostic view analyzes short- and medium-term spending trajectory and drivers:

  • Controls: Select an End month, rolling Window (6, 12, or 24 months), Breakdown dimension (Category, Payee, or Account), Rows (Top 5, Top 8, or Top 12), and Currency mode (Default converted currency vs. Actual transaction currency with an optional single-currency filter when multiple currencies appear).
  • Charts & Insights:
  • Expense Trajectory: Monthly spending curve overlaid with a 3-month rolling average.
  • Summary Cards: Latest Month vs. previous month, Range Highlights (High, Low, Window Average), and Volatility & Trend (Coefficient of Variation = StdDev / Mean, flagged as Low <15%, Moderate 15–30%, or High >30%).
  • Top Movers Variance and Distribution Composition charts for the selected dimension.
  • MoM Delta diverging bar chart plus Monthly Timeline and Breakdown tables with per-row sparklines.

docs.title: Year-over-Year (YoY)
docs.text:
Route: /expense/yoy

The Year-over-Year (YoY) view compares calendar years side-by-side (legacy /analysis/yoy redirects here):

  • Controls: Compare 2 to 5 years ending at a chosen Until year, and export the comparison table via Download CSV.
  • KPI Strip: Summarizes Spending, Income, Net savings, Savings rate (with top expense category), Biggest mover, and Efficiency snapshot.
  • Visualizations: Spending YoY, Income YoY, and Category YoY (with line/bar toggle), alongside Category Movers and Monthly Net Profile tables.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Track planned vs. actual monthly allocations in Budget.
  • Inspect full cash movements in Cash Flow.

docs.title: FX Rates
docs.text:
Open Ledger → FX Rates (/ledger/fx-rates) in either Grouped or Classic navigation to track foreign currency exchange rates and inspect your portfolio's currency exposure.

Paisa supports tracking multiple currencies and calculating the value of foreign assets in your default currency.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Currency Exposure Breakdown: A donut chart at the top of the page (and on Allocation Targets) summarizes your holdings by native currency versus your default_currency.
  • Daily Exchange Rates & Filters: Filter rates by Base currency, Quote currency, Year, and Month.
  • Direct vs. Derived (Cross) Rates: Each daily row is tagged as Direct (from a provider or journal entry) or Derived when Paisa synthesizes a missing pair via a one-hop cross rate through default_currency (for example, USD → INR → EUR).
  • Provider & Journal Prioritization: Exchange rates can be sourced from external price providers (such as Yahoo Finance) or directly from your journal entries. When a rate exists in both, the journal's implicit exchange rate takes precedence.
  • Reporting Currency & FX Impact: Across Balance, Net Worth, Expenses, and Prices views, report_currency selectors let you re-denominate reports, while Net Worth History breaks changes down into organic asset movement vs. FX rate movement (FX Impact Decomposition).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
To ensure Paisa treats commodities as currencies rather than securities (such as mutual funds or stocks), add them to the currencies list under Tools → Configuration → General → Display & Format (/more/config/display-format) or in paisa.yaml:

default_currency: INR
currencies:
  - USD
  - EUR

Once configured, price entries and multi-currency postings populate the FX Rates page and convert foreign balances into your default currency. If you need to fall back to single-currency price matching only, enable disable_multi_currency_prices: true under Tools → Configuration → Tools → Advanced (/more/config/advanced).

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Route: /ledger/import (Ledger → Import)

Paisa lets you import bank and credit card statements in CSV, TXT, OFX, QFX, XLS, XLSX, or PDF format directly into your journal. The Import page supports two modes:

  1. Smart Ingestion & Reconciliation (default) — automatic column detection, custom column mapping, rule-based and TF-IDF account categorization, duplicate flagging, and direct commit to your journal.
  2. Classic Template Editor — Handlebars template-based conversion with live preview and file export.

Experimental

PDF support is in an experimental stage and may not accurately detect rows on complex layouts.

docs.title: 1. Upload Statement
docs.text: Drag and drop any .csv, .txt, .ofx, .qfx, .xls, .xlsx, or .pdf file into the upload dropzone. Paisa parses the statement (POST /api/import/statement), extracts candidate transactions, and detects the source bank or card account from header/footer text (including built-in hints for accounts matching kotak/811, icici, axis, hdfc, and sbi as well as your existing chart of accounts).

docs.title: 2. Custom Column Mapping (Map Columns)
docs.text:
If a CSV, Excel, or PDF statement uses non-standard column headers or multi-row bank banners:

  • Click Map Columns (this modal also opens automatically if auto-detection finds zero transactions).
  • Select the Header Row from the first 12 rows of the file.
  • Map Date Column (required), Description / Payee Column, Amount Format (Separate Debit & Credit columns or Single Amount column + optional Dr/Cr indicator), and optional Currency Column.
  • Click Apply & Parse (or Reset to Auto-Detect to clear overrides).

docs.title: 3. Visual Rule Studio & Account Suggestions
docs.text:
Paisa categorizes each staged transaction in order of confidence:

  1. User Classification Rules (Rule Studio): Click Rule Studio (GET/POST/DELETE /api/rules) to define priority-ordered rules matching payee or memo patterns (contains, exact, or regex) and optional transaction direction (any, debit, credit), assigning a target account, tags, and an optional Flag for Review marker. You can also save rules inline from any staged transaction row via Quick Save Rule.
  2. Historical Payee & Merchant Taxonomy: Matches normalized descriptions against your past ledger postings and a built-in merchant taxonomy.
  3. TF-IDF Similarity: Computes cosine similarity in the browser against your existing transactions to suggest the likeliest expense/income/liability account.

docs.title: 4. Duplicate Detection
docs.text: During ingestion, staged rows are scored against existing journal postings. Rows scoring 70 or higher (same amount, close date within 7 days, and matching payee/memo context) are flagged as Possible Duplicates and deselected by default so you do not accidentally double-import an already recorded transaction.

docs.title: 5. Review & Commit to Ledger
docs.text:
1. Select your Source / Bank Account (e.g., Assets:Checking:ICICI or Liabilities:CreditCard:Freedom).
  2. Check or uncheck staged transactions and adjust any target accounts.
  3. Click Review & Commit to open Review Generated Ledger Entries, where you can inspect or edit the generated transactions and toggle Club debits by date (groups multiple same-day debits into one consolidated multi-posting transaction for Ledger/hledger; skipped automatically for Beancount).
  4. Click Confirm & Append to Ledger (POST /api/import/commit) to append the entries to add_journal_path (falling back to journal_path when add_journal_path is not configured) and validate the journal. Remember to Sync Journal afterward so the newly appended transactions appear across reports.

docs.title: Part 2: Classic Template Editor
docs.text:
Switch to Classic Template Editor at the top of the Import page if you prefer declarative Handlebars templates for full structural control over generated transactions. The classic interface has three components:

  1. File Preview – Drag and drop CSV/TXT/XLS/XLSX/PDF files to preview raw tabular rows.
  2. Ledger Preview – Live rendered ledger output.
  3. Template Editor – Edit the Handlebars template.

Each row in the file is processed against the template:

{{#if (and (isDate ROW.A "DD/MM/YYYY") (isBlank ROW.G))}}
 {{date ROW.A "DD/MM/YYYY"}} {{ROW.C}}
    {{predictAccount prefix="Expenses"}}        {{ROW.F}} INR
    Assets:Checking
{{/if}}

This converts a matching row into a transaction such as:

2023/03/28 AMAZON HTTP://WWW.AM IN
    Expenses:Shopping       249.00 INR
    Assets:Checking

docs.title: Template Management
docs.text: Paisa ships with built-in templates and lets you create custom ones with Save As (stored in paisa.yaml under import_templates).

docs.title: Template Data
docs.text:
1. ROW – The current row being processed. Columns are keyed by letters (ROW.A, ROW.B, …) and ROW.index holds the 0-based row index.
Example 
{
  "A": "28/03/2023",
  "B": "7357680821",
  "C": "AMAZON HTTP://WWW.AM IN",
  "D": "12",
  "E": "0",
  "F": "249.00",
  "G": "",
  "index": 6
}
  1. SHEET – The entire parsed sheet as an array of row objects (e.g., SHEET.5.A).
Example 
[
    {
        "A": "Accountno:",
        "B": "49493xxx003030",
        "index": 0
    },
    {
        "A": "Customer Name:",
        "B": "MR John Doe",
        "index": 1
    },
    {
        "A": "Address:",
        "B": "1234, ABC Street, XYZ City, 123456",
        "index": 2
    },
    {
        "A": "Transaction Details:",
        "index": 3
    },
    {
        "A": "Date",
        "B": "Sr.No.",
        "C": "Transaction Details",
        "D": "Reward Point Header",
        "E": "Intl.Amount",
        "F": "Amount(in Rs)",
        "G": "BillingAmountSign",
        "index": 4
    },
    {
        "A": "49493xxx003030",
        "index": 5
    },
    {
        "A": "28/03/2023",
        "B": "7357680821",
        "C": "AMAZON HTTP://WWW.AM IN",
        "D": "12",
        "E": "0",
        "F": "249.00",
        "G": "",
        "index": 6
    },
    {
        "A": "28/03/2023",
        "B": "7357821997",
        "C": "AMAZON HTTP://WWW.AM IN",
        "D": "28",
        "E": "0",
        "F": "575.00",
        "G": "",
        "index": 7
    }
]

docs.title: eq(a: any, b: any): boolean
docs.text: Checks if the two values are equal.

docs.title: not(value: any): boolean
docs.text: Negates the given value.

docs.title: and(...args: any[]): boolean
docs.text: Returns true if all the arguments are true.

docs.title: or(...args: any[]): boolean
docs.text: Returns true if any of the arguments are true.

docs.title: gte(a: string | number, b: string | number): boolean
docs.text: Checks if a is greater than or equal to b.

docs.title: gt(a: string | number, b: string | number): boolean
docs.text: Checks if a is greater than b.

docs.title: lte(a: string | number, b: string | number): boolean
docs.text: Checks if a is less than or equal to b.

docs.title: lt(a: string | number, b: string | number): boolean
docs.text: Checks if a is less than b.

docs.title: negate(value: string | number): number
docs.text: Negates the given value. For example, negate("123.45") returns -123.45.

docs.title: amount(str: string, {default?: string}): string
docs.text: Converts the given string to a valid amount. If blank, uses default. Examples: (0.9534) → -0.9534, ₹ 1,234.56 → 1234.56.

docs.title: round(str: string, {precision?: number}): number
docs.text: Rounds the given value to precision decimal places (defaults to 0).

docs.title: isDate(str: string, format: string): boolean
docs.text: Checks if str is a valid date in format (see Day.js format tokens).

docs.title: predictAccount(...terms: string[], {prefix?: string}): string
docs.text:
Finds transactions in your journal with similar descriptions and picks the top matching account. If terms are omitted, the entire ROW is used. prefix filters candidate accounts; returns Unknown if no match is found.

{{predictAccount prefix="Income"}}
{{predictAccount ROW.C ROW.F prefix="Income"}}

docs.title: isBlank(str: string): boolean
docs.text: Checks if the given string is blank.

docs.title: date(str: string, format: string): string
docs.text: Parses str using format and returns YYYY/MM/DD.

docs.title: findAbove(column: string, {regexp?: string}): string
docs.text:
Finds the first non-empty cell above the current row in column (optionally matching regexp).

{{findAbove B regexp="LIMITED"}}

docs.title: findBelow(column: string, {regexp?: string}): string
docs.text:
Finds the first non-empty cell below the current row in column (optionally matching regexp).

{{findBelow B regexp="LIMITED"}}

docs.title: acronym(str: string): string
docs.text: Returns an acronym suitable for a commodity symbol (e.g., UTI Nifty Next 50 Index Growth Direct Plan → UNNI).

docs.title: trim(str: string): string
docs.text: Trims leading and trailing whitespace.

docs.title: replace(str: string, search: string, replace: string): string
docs.text: Replaces search with replace inside str.

docs.title: regexpTest(str: string, regexp: string): boolean
docs.text: Tests whether str matches regexp.

docs.title: regexpMatch(str: string, regexp: string, {group?: number}): string
docs.text: Extracts a capture group (default 0): {{regexpMatch ROW.C "(.*) Growth Direct Plan" group=1}}.

docs.title: textRange(fromColumn: string, toColumn: string, {separator?: string}): string
docs.text:
Joins columns from fromColumn through toColumn with separator (defaults to " ").

{{textRange A C separator=" "}}

docs.title: toLowerCase(str: string): string
docs.text: Converts str to lowercase.

docs.title: toUpperCase(str: string): string
docs.text: Converts str to uppercase.

docs.title: capitalize(str: string): string
docs.text: Capitalizes str.

docs.title: match(str: string, {[string]: string}): string
docs.text:
Matches str against a map of Account="regex" pairs:

{{or (match ROW.C Expenses:Shopping="Amazon|Flipkart" Expenses:Groceries="BigBasket")
     "Expenses:Unknown"}}

docs.title: Import Preview (Template Mode)
docs.text: Click Preview to run POST /api/import/preview in dry-run mode. Paisa shows a row-by-row validation table with valid/invalid badges, error messages, and per-row selection checkboxes before saving output to a journal file.

docs.title: Import Presets
docs.text:
Frequently used delimiter/column configurations can be saved as named presets (GET/POST/DELETE /api/import/presets) in Paisa's SQLite database. Built-in presets cannot be deleted:

Preset Name Format description Generic Bank CSV Simple date / description / amount CSV Chase Credit Card CSV Chase card statement CSV export SBI Account Statement CSV State Bank of India account statement ICICI Credit Card CSV ICICI Bank credit card statement Kotak Bank Statement CSV Kotak Mahindra Bank account statement

Custom Handlebars templates can also be configured in paisa.yaml:

import_templates:
  - name: My Bank Statement
    content: |
      {{#if (isDate ROW.A "DD/MM/YYYY")}}
        {{date ROW.A "DD/MM/YYYY"}} {{ROW.C}}
          {{predictAccount prefix="Expenses"}}    {{amount ROW.F}} INR
          Assets:Checking
      {{/if}}

docs.title: Income
docs.text:
The Income section tracks your earnings over time and separates passive investment payouts (dividends, interest, and distributions) from earned income.

In the default Grouped navigation layout, these views are under Cash Flow → Income & Returns. In the Classic layout, they appear under the top-level Income menu.

docs.title: Income Timeline
docs.text:
Route: /income

The Income Timeline page shows:

  • Summary KPIs: Gross Income, Net Tax (Expenses:Tax:*), and TTM Investment Income (trailing 12 months).
  • Monthly Income Timeline: Stacked monthly bar chart across all Income:* accounts.
  • Financial Year Income Timeline: Side-by-side yearly totals for total income, net income (after taxes), and net taxes.

docs.title: Investment Income
docs.text:
Route: /income/investment

The Investment Income page (backed by GET /api/income/investment) analyzes passive returns by holding and income category:

  • Financial Year Picker: View trailing 12-month (TTM) metrics as of the current date or the end of a historical financial year.
  • KPI Strip: Displays TTM Investment Income, Dividend (TTM), Interest (TTM), and Distribution (TTM).
  • Per-Holding Breakdown Table: Lists each holding and payout type along with Total Income, TTM Income, Current Balance, TTM Yield (TTM Income / Current Balance), and a Dividend Growth sparkline.
  • Monthly Timeline: Visualizes investment income payouts over time.

A compact Investment Income widget (showing TTM Dividend and TTM Interest) is also available on the Dashboard.

docs.title: Account Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Paisa classifies investment income automatically from standard account prefixes (see Accounts):

  • Income:Dividend:* — stock and fund dividends
  • Income:Interest:* — savings, fixed deposit, EPF, or bond interest
  • Income:Distribution:* or Income:Distributions:* — REIT/fund distributions

Investment income also feeds into Assets → Gain (/assets/gain) to compute Income Received, Total Return (Price Appreciation + Income Received), and per-account TTM Yield.

docs.title: Journal
docs.text:
All your transactions are stored in plain text files called journal. You can organize your transactions into multiple journal files. The journal_path configuration refers your main journal file. The main journal file can refer other journal files using include directive. The include directive supports wildcards * as well. Transactions are sourced only from the main journal file and other journal files included from the main journal file.

include investments.ledger
include expenses/*.ledger

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: Paisa comes with a journal editor. It allows you to edit all the files with the same file extension as your main journal and in the same or sub directories as your main journal.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Paisa tries its best to keep your journal safe. Every time you save in the editor, it creates a backup of your journal file with a .backup.{timestamp} extension so you can revert to older versions or delete old backups directly from the editor. When editing journals outside Paisa, JournalWatcher automatically monitors your files and flags the navbar Sync indicator if a change needs to be re-synced.

You can also download a complete .zip archive of your journal files, paisa.yaml (with account password hashes redacted by default), and .sheet files from Tools → Configuration → Tools → Backup & Export (/more/config/backup).

Warning

It is recommended to keep your journal files and paisa.yaml under version control or other backup mechanism. Paisa's backup mechanism is not a replacement for a proper backup. You can ignore paisa.db file from your version control system, the data in db file can be recreated from your journal files.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: The journal syntax of the features you use normally along with paisa is documented here. Refer ledger documentation for more details.

docs.title: Transaction
docs.text:
2022/01/01 Salary
    Income:Salary:Acme      -100,000 INR
    Assets:Checking          100,000 INR

A transaction should start with a date followed by description. Following that you can have 2 or more postings. The posting line should have at least 2 leading spaces. The account name and the amount should be separated by at least 2 spaces.

docs.title: Commodity
docs.text:
2022/01/07 Investment
    Assets:Checking         -20,000 INR
    Assets:Equity:NIFTY   168.690 NIFTY @ 118.56 INR

commodity cost can be specified using the @ syntax. Here 118.56 is the per unit cost and 168.690 is the quantity you have bought.

docs.title: Comment
docs.text:
2023/07/01 Rent
    ; This is a transaction comment
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking   ; This is a posting comment

Any text after ; is treated as a comment. Comment can be at whole transaction level or individual posting level. Comment is also referred as note in many places, both are same.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
2023/07/01 Rent
    ; Recurring: Rent
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking

Transactions can be tagged with extra metadata called tags. Tag has two parts: tag name and value. In the above example, Recurring is the name and Rent is the value. Tag should be inside comment.

docs.title: Include
docs.text:
include investments.ledger
include expenses/*.ledger

Include directive can be used to include other journal files. It supports wildcards *.

docs.title: Natural Language Quick Add
docs.text:
Click the + (Quick Add Transaction) button in the top-right action strip (or press Ctrl+K → Quick Add Transaction) to capture new entries from free-form text or a structured form targeting add_journal_path. For example:

20 Apr, bought 15$ groceries using bmo cc from no frills

The parser extracts date, amount, currency, payee, and account candidates, lets you review confidence scores and candidate pills, and appends a validated journal entry. See the full API contract, request/response fields, and confidence handling in Natural Language Parser API.

docs.title: Ledger CLI
docs.text:
Paisa is compatible with ledger, hledger and beancount. By default paisa will try to use ledger, if you prefer to use hledger or beancount instead, change the ledger_cli value in paisa.yaml

# OPTIONAL, DEFAULT: ledger, ENUM: ledger, hledger, beancount
ledger_cli: hledger

Paisa ships with ledger binary. If you use hledger or beancount, make sure that the binaries are installed.

docs.title: Unavailable Features
docs.text: Some of the features that are available in Paisa are not supported by hledger and beancount

docs.title: hledger
docs.text: • Recurring (partial) - hledger supports automated transactions, but it doesn't allow to add only metadata to transaction. So some of the examples in the recurring section will not work with hledger. It's possible to add metadata to transactions manually.

docs.title: beancount
docs.text:
• Budget - budget relies on periodic transactions, which is not supported by beancount.

  • Recurring (partial) - beancount doesn't support automated transactions. It's possible to add metadata to transactions manually. Use lowercase for tag name.

  • Search filter in Transactions and Postings pages doesn't support note property.

docs.title: Dialect-Aware Features
docs.text:
Paisa adapts output and import formatting automatically to your configured ledger_cli:

  • Smart Importer & Quick Add: When writing entries for beancount, Paisa uses YYYY-MM-DD * "Payee" "Narration" syntax, #tag tags (instead of ; Tag: comments), and automatically skips group_by_date debit consolidation so multi-posting entries match Beancount conventions.
  • Price History Export: Both the Commodity Prices UI export and the paisa export CLI support --format ledger, --format hledger, and --format beancount (P vs. price directives).

docs.title: RFC: Multi-Currency Commodity Prices
docs.text: Status: Draft Date: 2026-03-18 Owner: Paisa Core Team

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Add first-class multi-currency commodity pricing across:

  1. Journal ingestion (ledger, hledger, beancount).
  2. External provider sync.
  3. Valuation and analytics.
  4. Price export back to ledger-family formats.

The current system stores one value per commodity and effectively treats it as quoted in default currency. This RFC introduces explicit price pairs and quote currency support while preserving backward compatibility.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Ingest and persist commodity prices as base and quote currency pairs.
  2. Support valuation in default currency and arbitrary report currency.
  3. Preserve round-trip fidelity: DB -> export file -> sync.
  4. Keep existing users functional without immediate config changes.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
1. Real-time streaming FX pricing.
  2. Intraday tick-level pricing.
  3. Automated provider arbitration beyond deterministic precedence rules.

docs.title: Current Behavior and Gaps
docs.text:
1. Journal price parsing filters to default-currency targets for most directives.
  2. Provider prices are stored without explicit quote currency.
  3. Price lookup is keyed by commodity only, not pair.
  4. Currency helper behavior assumes a single default currency.

This leads to loss of non-default quote information and prevents native multi-currency valuation.

docs.title: Proposed Data Model
docs.text:
Add quote currency and source metadata to the price model.

Proposed table shape:

  1. id
  2. date
  3. base_commodity
  4. quote_commodity
  5. rate
  6. source_type (journal | provider)
  7. source_provider (nullable)
  8. source_ref (nullable, provider code/ticker/scheme)
  9. created_at
  10. updated_at

Proposed uniqueness:

  1. unique(date, base_commodity, quote_commodity, source_type, source_provider, source_ref)

Recommended indexes:

  1. (base_commodity, quote_commodity, date)
  2. (quote_commodity, base_commodity, date)
  3. (source_type, source_provider)

Backward compatibility strategy:

  1. Existing rows without quote info are migrated with quote_commodity = default currency at migration time.

docs.title: Journal
docs.text:
1. Parse and keep all price directives (not only default-currency targets).
  2. Store directed pair base -> quote with rate.
  3. If parser receives the inverse pattern (for example default currency as commodity with foreign target), normalize into canonical base -> quote direction when deterministic.
  4. Preserve file date semantics and timezone behavior as today.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
1. Extend provider contract to return explicit quote_commodity.
  2. For providers already converting to default currency (for example some stock providers), either:
  3. keep conversion behavior but set quote_commodity explicitly, or
  4. store native quote + FX chain as separate pairs if available.
  5. For providers that return NAV in known local currency, set quote_commodity explicitly.

docs.title: Rate Resolution and Valuation
docs.text:
Introduce a pair-aware resolver:

  1. GetRate(base, quote, date) -> rate record.
  2. Resolution order:
  3. direct pair on or before date,
  4. inverse pair on or before date,
  5. optional one-hop cross via configured anchor currencies.
  6. Deterministic precedence when multiple sources exist on same date:
  7. journal overrides provider by default,
  8. tie-break by latest updated_at.

Valuation API behavior:

  1. Existing valuation endpoints continue to use default currency unless explicitly requested.
  2. New optional query parameter report_currency enables alternate report currency.

docs.title: Export Design
docs.text: Add export that writes DB prices to selected dialect format.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
1. dialect: ledger | hledger | beancount
  2. from_date (optional)
  3. to_date (optional)
  4. base_commodities (optional list)
  5. quote_commodities (optional list)
  6. source filter (optional)

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
1. ledger: P YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS BASE RATE QUOTE
  2. hledger: P YYYY-MM-DD BASE RATE QUOTE
  3. beancount: YYYY-MM-DD price BASE RATE QUOTE

Notes:

  1. Keep deterministic sort order by date, base, quote, source.
  2. Optionally emit source comments where dialect supports comments.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
1. GET /api/price
  2. add optional filters: base, quote, from, to, report_currency, source
  3. GET /api/price/export
  4. returns text output in requested dialect
  5. POST /api/price/export
  6. supports larger filter payloads and future options

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
1. paisa prices export --dialect ledger --from 2020-01-01 --to 2026-12-31 --base NIFTY --quote INR
  2. paisa prices export --dialect beancount --source journal > prices.beancount

docs.title: Phase 1: Schema and dual-write
docs.text:
1. Add new columns/table and migration.
  2. Read old model, write both old and new on sync.
  3. Add validation logs for pair completeness.

docs.title: Phase 2: Pair-aware reads
docs.text:
1. Switch service price resolution to pair-aware engine.
  2. Keep old read path behind fallback flag.

docs.title: Phase 3: API and UI
docs.text:
1. Add pair filters and report currency selector.
  2. Update price pages/charts for base/quote awareness.

docs.title: Phase 4: Export and cleanup
docs.text:
1. Ship dialect export endpoint and CLI command.
  2. Remove old single-commodity assumptions after compatibility window.

docs.title: Config Additions (Optional)
docs.text:
1. price_anchor_currencies: [USD, EUR]
  2. price_source_precedence:
  3. journal
  4. provider
  5. allow_cross_rate: true

Defaults should preserve current behavior for users who do not opt in.

docs.title: Testing Plan
docs.text:
1. Parser tests:
  2. ledger/hledger/beancount directives with mixed quote currencies.
  3. Migration tests:
  4. old DB upgrades and valuation parity in default currency mode.
  5. Resolver tests:
  6. direct, inverse, and cross-rate path resolution.
  7. precedence tie-breaking across journal and provider rows.
  8. Export tests:
  9. deterministic output snapshots for all dialects.
  10. Regression tests:
  11. existing snapshots remain valid in default settings.

docs.title: Rollout and Risk Management
docs.text:
1. Feature flag: enable_multi_currency_prices.
  2. Compatibility mode defaulted on for one release cycle.
  3. Telemetry/log counters for missing pairs and failed conversions.
  4. Clear fallback path to old resolver if severe issues are detected.

Primary risks:

  1. Ambiguous provider quote currency for some feeds.
  2. Performance regression from pair-aware lookups.
  3. Behavioral changes in historical valuation due to richer data.

Mitigations:

  1. Require quote currency from providers at ingestion boundary.
  2. Add indexed query plan checks and cache pair trees.
  3. Keep source precedence explicit and documented.

docs.title: Definition of Done
docs.text:
1. Multi-currency journal prices are persisted without dropping non-default quotes.
  2. Provider prices include explicit quote currency.
  3. Valuation works for default currency and requested report currency.
  4. Export works for ledger, hledger, and beancount formats.
  5. Existing users can upgrade without manual data edits.
  6. Regression suite passes with compatibility mode enabled and disabled.

docs.title: Decisions Locked
docs.text:
1. Source precedence: journal overrides provider.
  2. Cross-rate resolution: one hop only.
  3. Export default: full history.

docs.title: GitHub Issue Action Plan
docs.text: The items below are ready to be created as GitHub issues labeled enhancement.

docs.title: EPIC 1: Pair-Aware Price Schema and Migration
docs.text:
Suggested title: enhancement: add base/quote price schema with backward-compatible migration

Scope:

  1. Add pair-aware schema for prices with base commodity, quote commodity, rate, and source metadata.
  2. Add indexes and uniqueness constraints for deterministic lookups.
  3. Add migration from existing rows to quote_commodity = default_currency.
  4. Keep compatibility mode for existing single-currency behavior.

Acceptance criteria:

  1. Existing databases migrate successfully without data loss.
  2. Existing valuations in default currency remain unchanged in compatibility mode.
  3. New pair-aware rows can be written and queried by date/base/quote.

Dependencies:

  1. None.

Estimate:

  1. 3-5 engineering days.

docs.title: EPIC 2: Journal Ingestion for Full Price Pairs
docs.text:
Suggested title: enhancement: ingest full multi-currency journal price directives

Scope:

  1. Update ledger/hledger/beancount price parsers to retain non-default quote pairs.
  2. Normalize parsed prices into canonical base -> quote direction.
  3. Persist journal prices with source metadata (source_type = journal).
  4. Add parser fixtures for mixed quote currencies.

Acceptance criteria:

  1. Non-default quote prices are no longer dropped during sync.
  2. Same input journal produces deterministic base/quote output rows.

  3. Enforce source precedence rule: journal overrides provider.

Acceptance criteria:
